invariants.description: i_Na equals the Paci 2013 expression transcribed from the authors' CellML: fast Na current I_Na = TTX_coeff g_Na m^3 h j (Vm - E_Na)
invariants.expr: np.max(np.abs(i_Na - (np.where(TTX_3uM==1, 0.18, np.where(TTX_10uM==1, 0.06, np.where(TTX_30uM==1, 0.02, 1)))*g_Na*m**3*h*j*(Vm - E_Na)))) <= 1e-9*max(1.0, np.max(np.abs(np.where(TTX_3uM==1, 0.18, np.where(TTX_10uM==1, 0.06, np.where(TTX_30uM==1, 0.02, 1)))*g_Na*m**3*h*j*(Vm - E_Na))))

invariants.description: i_Na is outward (>= 0) above E_Na and inward below

bc_sweep.rationale: Clamp inputs span the physiological operating range of a hiPSC-CM: Vm -100 to +50 mV, reversal potentials +/-30 mV about their resting values, gates over [0, 1], Cai 1e-5 to 1e-3 mM, Nai 5-20 mM, extracellular concentrations +/-50 %, T room to body temperature; drug switches 0/1; conductances by the default factors 0.5-2. R and F are physical constants (not swept).

baseline.reason: candidate: the hiPSC-CM I-V / conductance data the current was fitted to (Ma et al. 2011, Am J Physiol Heart Circ Physiol 301:H2006, as used by Paci 2013) could be digitised and compared with the clamped steady-state current (gates at their steady state); needs the gate components composed with this one and owner approval of digitised data.

calibrate.note: pending: the maximal conductance could be identified from the same I-V data once a baseline is agreed.
